solution: Write ${=b}$ as a power whose exponent is ${=n}$, the denominator of the exponent: ${=b}={=r}^{{=n}}$.
notes: Entry point of the skill: a whole-number base that is a perfect n-th power, positive exponent m/n in lowest terms (n is 2 or 3, m is 1 to 3). Same chain as the book's 27^(-1/3): write the base as a power, multiply the exponents. Cases are 4^(1/2) up to 144^(1/2), 8^(1/3) up to 125^(1/3), 4^(3/2) and 25^(3/2) (125), and 8^(2/3) up to 125^(2/3). 23 distinct instances, answers at most 125. The root r may be composite (36 = 6^2, 64 = 4^3), as the book itself does in ex2-4-3i.
